core_meaning.short_meaning: Trustee or disposer of affairs; a divine name in the Qur'an
core_meaning.primary_meaning: Wakil (الوكيل) is a divine name meaning “the Trustee” or “the One who disposes of affairs”. It occurs in the Qur'an in verses such as 3:173, 4:81, 28:28, 33:3, 39:62 and 73:9. In ordinary Arabic, wakīl also means a representative or attorney, and the word is used as a male given name.
core_meaning.literal_meaning: Trustee, representative, or disposer of affairs
core_meaning.meaning_explanation: Arabic lexicography records wakīl as the person to whom a matter is entrusted, from the root و ك ل. The Qur'anic divine name الوكيل expresses God's sufficiency and disposal of affairs. Using it as a personal name is a Muslim naming convention; it does not attribute divinity to the bearer.
